c.tagline: Aegean gateway of seafront promenades, seafood and easy sunshine.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered; book through the BiTaksi or municipal iTaksi apps, and Uber in İzmir dispatches licensed taxis rather than private cars.

emergency.note: 112 is Türkiye's unified emergency number for police, ambulance, and fire.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing around Konak/Kemeraltı bazaar and the seafront

hood_desc: İzmir's lively, bohemian heart in the Konak district, lined with restaurants, bars, boutiques and the palm-fringed Kordon seafront promenade that fills with outdoor cafes at sunset; best for young travelers who want nightlife and dining within walking distance.

The historic and commercial center around the Clock Tower (Saat Kulesi), the sprawling Kemeraltı Bazaar and the ancient Agora; the main transport hub with metro, tram, ferry and bus links, ideal for first-timers who want everything walkable.

A relaxed, upscale seaside district across the bay from Konak with a long waterfront, parks, shopping and a laid-back local feel; superbly linked by ferry, train and tram and popular with families wanting calm and sea views.

A leafy district on the eastern side of the city home to Ege University and a large student population, with lively cafes, budget eats and green campus grounds; suits younger travelers and those wanting an authentic, affordable base.

A coastal suburban stretch southwest of the center known for the Balçova thermal springs, the Balçova teleferik (cable car), marinas and quiet residential seafront living; suits travelers wanting a calm, scenic base away from the crowds.

water.note: Tap water is chlorinated but most locals drink bottled; bottled is the safer choice.

transit.hours: The Metro runs roughly 06:00 to 00:20 with trains about every 5 minutes; trams, İZBAN and ferries run daytime to late evening, with ESHOT night buses covering the overnight gap.
transit.note: İzmir's transport wraps around the bay: a single Metro line plus three tram lines (Konak, Karşıyaka and Buca), the İZBAN suburban railway spanning Aliağa to the airport, an extensive ESHOT bus network, and İZDENİZ passenger ferries that cross the harbour between Konak, Karşıyaka, Bostanlı and other quays.
transit.pay: Tap a single rechargeable İzmirimKart across the Metro, trams, İZBAN, ferries and buses, with cheap transfers between them; buy and top up cards at station machines and kiosks. Single rides cost well under US$1 with the card.

transit.m: İZBAN suburban train to Alsancak / city center (~30-40 min, every 10-20 min)
Havaş / ESHOT airport bus to the center (~40 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% at restaurants for good service is appreciated but not expected.
